EO 13792 (signed 2017-04-26, 82 FR 20429-20431), read in full from the held FR text, orders the Secretary of the Interior to review Antiquities Act monument designations made since 1996 (sec. 2(a)-(c)) and report to the President, an interim report within 45 days and a final report within 120 days (sec. 2(d)-(e)). The machine own-term kinds are report_deadline (sec. 2(d), 2(e)) and condition (sec. 3(b)). A report deadline is never an end; the order has no sunset or termination wording, so every clause remains part of the order until revoked. No clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked on the report-deadline question; the producer does not claim when either report was delivered. EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(a) revokes it, effective on signing, 2021-01-20. The dossier lists no missing provision and no other actor provision; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original texts finds EO 13792 named only in EO 13990. The monument-boundary proclamations of 2017 were separate Presidential acts, not part of this order. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but name none of the six orders and reinstate nothing. Inventory: the dossier's 18 clauses cover the operative text from sec. 1 through sec. 3(c); its scope labels for sec. 2(a)(v)-(vii) ('sec2-v', 'sec2-v-vi', 'sec2-v-vii') are irregular but each span is correct and no text is missing or duplicated.

rationales.exact_text: Reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json (EO 13990, 86 FR 7037-7043, read once in full): sec. 7(a) revokes EO 13792 with no savings, pending-matter or transition clause; sec. 8(a) saves only statutory agency authority; sec. 7(f) tells the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind issuances implementing or enforcing the revoked orders; nothing is transferred. Own-residual check, reading EO 13792 in full: it orders a review of national monument designations and two reports and creates no right, benefit, property or fund (sec. 3(c) disclaims rights); it designates, modifies and withdraws nothing itself. Any later Presidential proclamation about monument boundaries was a separate act under the Antiquities Act, and EO 13990 sec. 3 reviews those proclamations on its own terms, so none is a surviving effect of this order. finding.analysis: The exact rationale treats a performed one-time command as necessarily operative until revocation because the order has no express termination-on-performance wording. The current pinned owner ruling instead requires separating a command exhausted by established use/performance from surviving consequences. DOI testimony supplies affirmative interim-submission evidence, rather than merely a missed or elapsed deadline. That makes the categorical premise inadequate to sustain this first-end conclusion. Receipt, routing and completeness limitations prevent adopting the testimony date, the 45-day deadline, or any invented date as the exact first end; they do not erase the evidence that interim submission occurred.
finding.applicability: EO13792 sec2(d) independently requires an interim report to the President through four specified executive officials within 45 days, covering Bears Ears and any other designations selected by the Secretary, with recommendations. DOI testimony identifies a submitted Interim Report specifically addressing Bears Ears, making actual performance relevant to this exact one-time command.

finding.earlier_ending: The dated January 30, 2018 DOI statement affirmatively says the Secretary submitted two reports to the President and identifies the first as the Interim Report. It supports actual interim-report submission by that date, earlier than the claimed January 20, 2021 first end. The 45-day term proves a deadline, not delivery. This supports re-examining exhaustion by performance without proving an exact first cessation date or complete required routing.

finding.independent_commands: The separate final-report duty in sec2(e) is not discharged merely by interim submission. The review and associated consultation commands in sec2(a)-(c), the policy, and general implementation qualifications require separate scope/performance examination. Interim reporting is not evidence that all EO13792 commands ceased.
finding.method: Fresh source examination of exact held EO13792 text, DOI final-report PDF/raw and text, and DOI testimony HTML/raw and text; final-report PDF pages 1 and 3 rendered and visually inspected; apply the exact pinned 2026-10-28 owner ruling to the separately identified reporting duty. No raw-original authentication or complete whole-case review asserted.
finding.rationale_span: a performed command stays part of the order until it is revoked
finding.savings: Sec3 preserves statutory agency authority and OMB functions, requires lawful implementation subject to appropriations, and disclaims enforceable rights. Those qualifications do not prove continued operation of an already performed interim-report duty. Conversely, possible later recommendations, monument actions or statutory consequences cannot be extinguished merely by identifying interim submission.
finding.scope: Only /operative_clauses/11/first_end is nominated for revalidation from the unsupported premise in its own judgment_reason. The interim-report duty is examined independently of sec2(e); a final-report memorandum alone would not establish that the interim duty occurred. No replacement first end or whole-order/status conclusion is adopted.
finding.source_examination_limitations: Original raw PDF absent; original held text verified by hash. No exact report delivery/receipt date, replacement first end, whole-order cessation or status change established. This is an AI methodological review, never human certification.
finding.unresolved_question: The interim report itself is absent from the reviewed inputs. Its complete mandated contents, actual delivery/receipt date and passage through the OMB Director, Economic and Domestic Policy Assistants and CEQ Chairman remain unverified. What event and supported interval exhausted the precise sec2(d) obligation, including its required recipients/routing?
